title_en:
@BLKMDL3 @wholemars In case anyone is curious:

We’ve had a ~pixel-perfect world model since last year, which is critical for synthetic data generation. 

The (much) smaller version of that in the car is a conditional mean-flow model, based on the recent sequence of Tesla Universal Vision Encoder features, which are the same ones that are plugged into the 3B encoder model that produces the driving actions. 

We fork off from these UVE features, then run a separate ~1B diffusion model. This takes in the previous reality-view generation with added noise and then denoises it to the current visualization. 

It then produces a small video chunk (8 images at 36 fps, at the resolution of the UI screen). This work is done by 1/2 of a TRIP engine every UVE frame at 18 hz and is spread over 4 cycles. 

Currently, the latency is a bit high due to compute constraints, but we have ways to interleave newer UVE features along the diffusion transformer layers to cut roughly 35% of the latency.

@BLKMDL3 @wholemars 如果有人好奇：

自去年以来，我们已经有了一个像素完美的世界模型，这对于合成数据的生成至关重要。

汽车中的（小得多）版本是条件平均流模型，基于 Tesla 通用视觉编码器功能的最新序列，这些功能与插入到产生驾驶动作的 3B 编码器模型中的功能相同。

我们从这些 UVE 功能中分叉出来，然后运行一个单独的 ~1B 扩散模型。这会吸收先前生成的添加了噪声的现实视图，然后将其降噪到当前的可视化中。

Elysium operates with 100ms block i
title_en:
The first block tells a bigger story about @Hypesium than a simple speed benchmark.

Elysium operates with 100ms block intervals and no public mempool. That changes the way applications need to approach transaction preparation. In a conventional workflow, several operations may happen after an opportunity appears. On Elysium, moving that work earlier becomes an important architectural decision.

Hypesium describes a preparation-first execution model:

➜ The transaction route is constructed in advance.
➜ Calldata is prepared before the pool event.
➜ Gas information is refreshed.
➜ Wallet nonce state is maintained.
➜ The pool creation log triggers the submission process.

The documented hot path targets under 5ms, with four communication lanes used for simultaneous submission.

What I find interesting is the relationship between block timing and software architecture. A 100ms block interval doesn't simply reward faster computers. It also rewards systems that minimize the amount of work left for the final moment.

There is still a distinction between transaction submission, block inclusion and final confirmation. These should never be treated as identical performance measurements.

@Hypesium's architecture offers an interesting case study in moving computation away from a time-sensitive execution window.

The real engineering question is not just how quickly a system reacts, but how much preparation it completes before there is anything to react to.

full_text_zh:
第一个块讲述了关于 @Hypesium 的更大故事，而不是简单的速度基准。

Elysium 以 100 毫秒的区块间隔运行，没有公共内存池。这改变了应用程序处理事务准备的方式。在传统的工作流程中，机会出现后可能会发生多个操作。在 Elysium 上，提前移动该工作成为一个重要的架构决策。

Hypesium 描述了一种准备优先的执行模型：

➜ 交易路径是提前构建的。
➜ Calldata 在池事件之前准备好。
➜ 气体信息被刷新。
➜ 维持钱包随机数状态。
➜ 池创建日志触发提交过程。

记录的热路径目标为 5 毫秒以下，并使用四个通信通道同时提交。

我发现有趣的是块时序和软件架构之间的关系。 100 毫秒的区块间隔不仅仅奖励更快的计算机。它还奖励那些最大限度地减少最后时刻剩余工作量的系统。

交易提交、区块包含和最终确认之间仍然存在区别。这些绝不应该被视为相同的性能测量。

@Hypesium 的架构提供了一个有趣的案例研究，将计算从时间敏感的执行窗口中移开。

真正的工程问题不仅仅是系统的反应速度有多快，而是在做出反应之前它完成了多少准备工作。

title_en:
THE WINNER OF ANTHROPIC'S OFFICIAL HACKATHON HAS PUBLISHED HIS CLAUDE CODE SETUP AND IT'S PURE GOLD

68 subagents, 286 skills, 94 commands, MIT license.

ECC turns Claude Code into a full engineering team.

The plan comes before the code.

The failing test comes before the fix.

Every change is reviewed by a context that hasn't seen how it was written.

→ Planning: you give it a sentence and approve the plan before a single line exists  
→ Review: a different reviewer per language that reads your diff from scratch  
→ Build fixes: a fixer per toolchain, including PyTorch and CUDA  
→ Security: full OWASP sweep and injection scanning in the agent config  
→ Architecture: detects design errors when they're still cheap, before migration  
→ Domain: databases, ML pipelines, E2E tests, and documentation

The security part is what almost nobody sets up.

An external OWASP audit costs four figures and a week. This one is ready before you eat.

The skills cover testing, Python, Go, Rust, Django, Next.js, Docker, and CI/CD.

That said, don't activate all 286 at once or you'll end up with a config worse than the one you had.

This is how it integrates well:

→ Make a fork and read the README before copying anything  
→ Start only with the planning agent and the rules pack for your main language  
→ Copy to your .claude folder only the agents and skills you're going to use this week  
→ Add the code reviewer and the security one afterward, as they yield the most  
→ Test it first on a small repo, not in production  
→ If something's extra, cut it. If you miss something, add just one more piece

The rule is simple: if you don't know what an agent is for, you don't need it yet.

title_en:
VIBE CODING DIDN'T CREATE A GENERATION OF BUILDERS. IT CREATED A GENERATION OF STARTERS.

MIT just published the most uncomfortable paper on AI coding.

They tracked every new app on the App Store, Play Store and Chrome Web Store after coding agents showed up.

Devs using autonomous agents wrote 25.5x more code.

Commits up 240%.

Actual releases?

Up 30%.

It gets worse.

After adopting tools like Claude Code, devs wrote 7x more lines and deleted 12.2x more.

Repos abandoned within 30 days went from 60% to 69%.

New apps launching roughly DOUBLED since early 2025.

User engagement didn't move.

Twice as many apps.

Same number of people using them.

I felt this one personally.

I shipped three "projects" last month with Claude Code.

Pretty sure zero humans used any of them.

Here's my take.

AI didn't make people better builders.

It made starting so cheap that finishing stopped meaning anything.

Writing code was never the bottleneck.

Taste was.

Reviewing was.

Building something people actually want was.

And no model is fixing that for you.

title_en:
HOLY F*CK... MIT students made $26 MILLION in ONE live round at a Citadel & Jane Street contest... from a single Python notebook that's on GitHub for free

3rd place, one notebook, the model Goldman Sachs built in 1990: Black-Litterman. no deep learning, no GPUs, just MATH

i ran their exact rule on 9 real stocks since October & let Claude Fable 5.2 make every call: the paper book is up 2.1% while SPY dropped 7.5%

first understand how this works:

> every team got the same stocks, live prices & 3 analysts' price predictions, then the contest scored the portfolios live

> Black-Litterman starts from what the market already holds & tilts toward the analysts, only as far as the math trusts them

> a Sharpe gate keeps a new portfolio only when it beats the current one, & the bot finished the live round $26 MILLION up

how to run it with Claude Code:

1. tell Claude Code to clone https://t.co/dhTzZnC1fI & open case3.ipynb

2. have it run the notebook on their case3data first (it was written for Colab, so Claude swaps the Google Drive paths for local ones)

3. ask Claude to swap in real stocks & real analyst price targets as the views, Yahoo has both

4. keep their Sharpe gate, so a new target only goes in when it beats the current book

5. run it once a day after the close & log every target to a csv

6. let Claude decide each rebalance, execute or hold, with a reason (that's what Fable 5.2 does in the video)

7. paper trade the book & compare it with SPY every week

8. cap any single short, the raw rule sometimes asks for 89% net short

9. move to a live account only after a few months of paper results you like

title_en:
🚨ALERT: U.S. banks are taking a HANDS-OFF approach to outside AI agents’ mistakes.

If you give an AI agent access to your account and it sends money to the wrong person, your bank may treat the payment as one you approved. 

And, you could be on the hook.

Here's what banks recently included in their terms:

- Citi says it will treat transfers as yours even if the agent ignores your instructions or someone uses a password the agent leaked.

- PNC requires bank-approved connections and generally bars outside agents from paying bills or moving money.

- Chase lets you share account data through approved connections but bars you from giving an outside AI tool your bank login.

- Bank of America advised customers to approve transfers themselves before an AI tool sends money, per TechCrunch.

- Schwab blocked AI tools that tried to move customers’ money without permission.

- Wells Fargo says that starting Nov. 24, it will treat an agent’s transfers as yours if you gave it access.

Yet, you can still dispute a transfer. Federal law may protect you depending on who sent the money and how they got access.

title_en:
‼️ A malicious webpage could make Muse, Meta's personal AI agent, send a user's private chats and stored memories to an outside server, without ever asking for approval.

Security research firm NebuSec showed it in a lab demo. The attack then broke out of Muse's sandbox into the user's cloud machine and reached the store where Muse keeps credentials.

Muse acts through the accounts users connect to it, and can make purchases for them.

NebuSec says Meta fixed the flaws before it published on 20 November. Meta has not commented, and it is not known whether any real user's data was accessed.

What happens when an AI
title_en:
One question will become increasingly important as AI agents move into industrial environments

What happens when an AI system makes a decision, executes an action, and something goes wrong?

Getting an AI to produce an accurate answer is one challenge. Making sure its actions are authorized, traceable, and accountable is an entirely different problem.

This is where I find @Actum_AI particularly interesting.

Its PoHA (Proof of Human Accountable Action) framework approaches AI trust from the perspective of behavioral accountability rather than relying solely on model performance.

The idea is to establish the rules before an action takes place, verify whether the action meets the required conditions, and preserve evidence that can be examined afterward.

Several parts of this architecture stand out to me.

First, the pre frozen codebook establishes permitted behavior in advance. An AI agent should not be able to redefine its own permissions while executing a task.

Second, six dimensional verification introduces multiple checkpoints, including time, location, personnel authorization, permitted actions, required elements, and execution sequence.

Third, the bi temporal ledger distinguishes when an event actually happened from when it was recorded. That distinction becomes extremely important when investigating operational incidents.

There is also the five state behavioral evidence model, which gives context to missing activity instead of automatically treating silence as proof that nothing happened.

What makes this approach more interesting is its industrial application. Actum reports that its infrastructure is already operating across thousands of endpoints and processing verified behavioral events in production environments.

The 8 patent filings and 5 software copyrights add another dimension to the project. They indicate an effort to establish and protect the underlying technology, although the real measure of its value will ultimately be how reliably the system performs in practice.

My takeaway is that enterprise AI adoption will require more than intelligence and automation.

Companies need to know what an agent was allowed to do, whether it followed the rules, and which human authority is accountable for the outcome.

AI can make decisions faster, but speed alone does not create trust.

The infrastructure behind those decisions matters just as much.

这就是我觉得@Actum_AI 特别有趣的地方。

其PoHA（人类责任行动证明）框架从行为责任的角度来处理人工智能信任，而不是仅仅依赖于模型性能。

其想法是在行动发生之前建立规则，验证行动是否满足所需条件，并保存事后可以检查的证据。

这个架构的几个部分对我来说很突出。

首先，预冻结码本预先建立允许的行为。 AI代理在执行任务时不应该能够重新定义自己的权限。

其次，六维验证引入了多个检查点，包括时间、地点、人员授权、允许的操作、所需的要素和执行顺序。

第三，双向账本区分事件实际发生的时间和记录的时间。在调查操作事件时，这种区别变得极其重要。

还有五状态行为证据模型，它为缺失的活动提供背景信息，而不是自动将沉默视为没有发生任何事情的证据。

让这种方法更有趣的是它的工业应用。 Actum 报告称，其基础设施已在数千个端点上运行，并在生产环境中处理经过验证的行为事件。

8 项专利申请和 5 项软件版权为该项目增添了另一个维度。它们表明了建立和保护底层技术的努力，尽管其价值的真正衡量标准最终将是系统在实践中执行的可靠性。

我的结论是，企业采用人工智能需要的不仅仅是智能和自动化。

公司需要知道代理人被允许做什么、是否遵守规则以及哪个权威机构对结果负责。

人工智能可以更快地做出决策，但仅靠速度并不能创造信任。

这些决策背后的基础设施同样重要。

title_en:
Moving an AI agent to another machine sounds simple. Keeping its memory and decisions intact is a different challenge.

This is an overlooked question worth exploring with @Acurast .

Imagine a trading agent running on a smartphone Processor. It tracks open positions, risk limits, and pending transactions.

If that Processor goes offline, restarting the same code elsewhere doesn't necessarily restore what the agent was doing.

That's the difference between code portability and state portability.

Acurast provides distributed, verifiable execution, but developers still need durable storage and recovery logic to preserve an agent's state across deployments.

To me, this is where decentralized AI infrastructure becomes more interesting.

Running an agent anywhere is useful. Making sure it can safely continue where it left off is what makes that flexibility practical.

Happy Sunday! Hope everyone is having a relaxing weekend.

I've been thinking about one practical challenge in the AI agent economy: how do we make sure agents understand exactly what they're expected to deliver?

Imagine hiring an AI agent to build a complete product. A vague instruction like "make it great" isn't enough.

The task needs a clear scope, defined deliverables, agreed pricing, and a way to evaluate the final result.

This is one reason I find @termix_ai interesting.

Through https://t.co/Bhy0UN0tK3, jobs can move through a structured process involving quotes, escrow, delivery, challenges, and settlement.

And with subcontracting, a lead agent can break a larger project into smaller tasks and bring in specialized agents to handle different parts.

To me, this is more than just connecting AI tools.

It's about creating a workflow where responsibilities and expectations are clear before work begins, while payments and outcomes have a defined process.

Of course, the quality of the final result still depends on good coordination and proper verification.

But as agents take on more complex work, clear task boundaries may become just as important as their intelligence.

A successful agent economy won't be built only on agents that can do more.

It will also need systems that help them work together reliably.

That's another part of @termix_ai I'm watching closely.

这是关于创建一个工作流程，在工作开始之前责任和期望是明确的，而付款和结果有一个明确的流程。

当然，最终结果的质量仍然取决于良好的协调和适当的验证。

但随着特工承担更复杂的工作，清晰的任务边界可能变得与他们的智力同样重要。

成功的代理经济并不仅仅建立在能做更多事情的代理之上。

它还需要帮助它们可靠地协同工作的系统。

这是我正在密切关注的@termix_ai 的另一部分。

❓ IS VOLARIS BACKING AWAY FROM FIVE NEW AIRBUS A321NEO DELIVERIES AMID FLEET RESTRUCTURING?

Mexican low-cost carrier Volaris is reportedly stepping back from taking delivery of five newly manufactured Airbus A321neo aircraft that were previously associated with its fleet expansion plans.

Aircraft production and tracking records indicate that the five aircraft, identified by their manufacturer serial numbers (MSNs), have been reassigned or associated with other airline customers.

The five aircraft involved:

✈️ MSN 13524 – Originally registered XA-WTB; subsequently associated with Iberia Express as EC-OYY.

✈️ MSN 13358 – Subsequently delivered to Aegean Airlines as SX-NBA.

✈️ MSN 13462 – Subsequently delivered to Aegean Airlines as SX-NAY.

✈️ MSN 13512 – Associated with Vietjet Air.

✈️ MSN 13579 – Originally registered XA-WTA; subsequently associated with Iberia Express as EC-OYZ.

Why is Volaris adjusting its fleet?

The development comes as Volaris undertakes a broader fleet and capacity restructuring amid financial pressures, aircraft availability challenges and ongoing Pratt & Whitney GTF engine-related maintenance issues.

In its third-quarter 2026 results, Volaris reported a fleet of 154 aircraft, with next-generation NEO models accounting for 71% of its total fleet.

The airline is also planning to remove approximately 17 aircraft between October 2026 and December 2027. 

Industry reports indicate that it has rescheduled 27 Airbus deliveries and postponed another 28 until 2032.

The reassignment of these five aircraft highlights how airlines and aircraft manufacturers are adjusting delivery schedules in response to changing fleet requirements, financial conditions and operational constraints.

While the aircraft reassignments are visible in production and tracking records, Volaris has not publicly confirmed that it formally rejected all five deliveries.

full_text_zh:
❓ 在机队重组过程中，Volaris 是否会放弃五架新空客 A321NEO 交付？

据报道，墨西哥低成本航空公司 Volaris 将不再接收五架新制造的空客 A321neo 飞机，这些飞机此前与其机队扩张计划有关。

飞机生产和跟踪记录表明，这五架飞机（通过制造商序列号（MSN）识别）已被重新分配或与其他航空公司客户相关联。

涉及的五架飞机：

✈️ MSN 13524 – 最初注册的XA-WTB；随后与 Iberia Express 关联为 EC-OYY。

✈️ MSN 13358 – 随后作为 SX-NBA 交付给爱琴海航空公司。

✈️ MSN 13462 – 随后以 SX-NAY 形式交付给爱琴海航空公司。

✈️ MSN 13512 – 与越捷航空相关。

✈️ MSN 13579 – 最初注册的XA-WTA；随后与 Iberia Express 关联为 EC-OYZ。

Volaris 为何要调整其机队？

这一进展正值 Volaris 在财务压力、飞机可用性挑战以及持续的普惠 GTF 发动机相关维护问题下进行更广泛的机队和运力重组之际。

Volaris 在 2026 年第三季度业绩中报告称，其机队拥有 154 架飞机，其中下一代 NEO 型号占其机队总数的 71%。

该航空公司还计划在 2026 年 10 月至 2027 年 12 月期间拆除约 17 架飞机。

行业报告显示，该公司已重新安排了 27 架空客飞机的交付，并将另外 28 架飞机的交付推迟到 2032 年。

这五架飞机的重新分配凸显了航空公司和飞机制造商如何调整交付时间表，以应对不断变化的机队需求、财务状况和运营限制。

虽然飞机的重新分配在生产和跟踪记录中可见，但 Volaris 尚未公开证实其正式拒绝了所有五架飞机的交付。

@daibond_alpha @du_yilun IMPORTANT NOTE: 
EBM are often presented as a particular form of probabilistic models. 
This is a very common misunderstanding. 
EBMs are *MORE GENERAL* than probabilistic models. 
Probabilistic models are a special case of EBMs in which:
1. Energies can be turned into a probabilities through the Gibbs distribution. That requires a convergent and computable partition function!
2. The loss function has a probabilistic interpretation, e.g. negative likelihood.

But there is whole world of EBMs that are NOT probabilistic: they require no partition function or normalization, and they can be trained with lots of loss functions that have no probabilistic interpretation.

title: most people know the usual model: you need something done, find an AI agent, give it instructions and let it handle the
title_en:
most people know the usual model: you need something done, find an AI agent, give it instructions and let it handle the task

but things get more interesting when that agent starts hiring other agents instead of doing everything itself

say you ask an agent to plan your trip to Bali, it can build the itinerary, compare hotels and estimate costs, but maybe it can't handle airport transportation

so it finds another agent that specializes in transport bookings and hires it to take care of that part

the first agent becomes the client, the second one is the provider. and in another deal, their roles could easily switch

that's a different kind of agent economy

agents need more than just a way to talk to each other. they need to discover services, agree on terms, fund orders, deliver the work and settle payments

that's the problem @termix_ai is trying to address with AACP, covering the workflow from discovery and offers to funded orders, delivery, disputes and settlement

one thing i think is important here: an agent isn't locked into being a client or provider. it can hire another agent in one transaction and provide a service in the next

of course, this doesn't mean agents can already do everything autonomously or spend money freely

users still control the permissions they grant, and onchain actions involving value still need wallet authorization

if agents can start hiring each other to get things done, the agent economy could grow beyond a bunch of AI tools and become a real service market between agents

not financial advice, DYOR

full_text_zh:
大多数人都知道通常的模式：你需要完成某件事，找到人工智能代理，给它指令并让它处理任务

但当该代理人开始雇用其他代理人而不是自己做所有事情时，事情会变得更有趣

假设您要求代理商计划您的巴厘岛之旅，它可以制定行程、比较酒店并估算费用，但也许它无法处理机场交通

因此，它找到了另一家专门从事交通预订的代理商，并聘请它来处理该部分

第一个代理成为客户，第二个代理成为提供商。在另一笔交易中，他们的角色可以轻松转换

这是一种不同类型的代理经济

代理需要的不仅仅是一种相互交谈的方式。他们需要发现服务、商定条款、为订单提供资金、交付工作并结算付款

这就是 @termix_ai 试图通过 AACP 解决的问题，涵盖从发现和报价到资助订单、交付、争议和解决的工作流程

我认为这里很重要的一件事是：代理不会被锁定为客户或提供商。它可以在一笔交易中雇用另一位代理人，并在下一笔交易中提供服务

当然，这并不意味着代理商已经可以自主完成所有事情或随意花钱

用户仍然控制自己授予的权限，涉及价值的链上操作仍然需要钱包授权

如果代理商可以开始互相雇佣来完成工作，那么代理商经济可能会超越一堆人工智能工具，并成为代理商之间真正的服务市场

title_en:
After more than 150 years of fascinating and torturing mathematicians, the most formidable problem in all of math may have finally fallen.

Today, Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at the #AI company Anthropic, posted a four-page paper on his personal website. “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” he wrote. Alpöge has not released the AI-generated explanation of the proof, which he says runs over 250,000 pages. But he provided 17 million lines of code that formally verify a broad version of the conjecture, called the generalized Riemann hypothesis, which extends Bernhard Riemann’s prediction about prime numbers to a wider family of mathematical functions.

Many mathematicians say they think Alpöge’s Riemann proof will hold up to scrutiny—and predict it will have far-reaching implications.

What’s far less clear is when—and if—mathematicians will manage to glean any understanding from the messy heap of code, which is larger than some entire computer operating systems. Learn more: https://t.co/YLtBEj1ScX

title_en:
Google recently announced Loop, its new self-improving AI agent that can autonomously work toward a given goal. 

Loop is internally called Jitro; interestingly, that was the exact name for Jules v2. 

Here is how it works 👀

1. Users start creating a Workspace by connecting it to a selected Github project and adding basic information. 

2. Users can create loops manually or select ones that are already predefined (ex., Harden Application Security)

"Custom Loops" can be created via a prompt or by manually filling in the Loop title, icon, and objective. 

> "Loops are mid- to long-term objectives for Stitch Loop to continuously work toward. They can range from highly specific to broad, but should always be something code can achieve," says the description. 

3. Users can connect additional context in the form of Integrations, Files, Links, or additional repositories.

More than 100 integrations are available there, including services like Jira, Linear, Datadog, Sentry, Notion, Snowflake, Salesforce, Intercom, Discord, Slack, Figma, and many others. 

Custom MCPs are supported as well. 

4. After creating a workspace, Loop will start digging into your project details and generate its own Skills about the product and product metrics. 

These Skills will live in a separate tab and can be edited in the UI in Markdown. 

5. When the Workspace is ready, Loop will suggest metrics and goals based on its own research. Users can convert these suggestions into loops right away. 

When a Loop is created, it appears as a running process in the main UI. 

6. When a Loop is finished, users will see a list of suggestions for every loop, along with a number associated with a target metric and progress status. 

Example Loop:
- Goal - Scale Telegram community contributions.
- KPIs - community members, registered contributors, active members. 

A high-level goal would be broken down into sub-KPIs. When users open a dedicated Loop page, all these KPIs will be visible on the dashboard.

Below, Users will see a list of Tasks, Skills, and Activity tabs. 

Example Task:
- Telegram channel lacks discussion threads and a dedicated bot.

Each task has a detailed description, labels, and the date when it was updated. Below, users will see tabs for Solutions, Activity, and Evidence. 

Activity appears as a summary describing what happened, what was done, and the general Timeline. 

Evidence contains links to where Loop pulled the context behind this Task. In my example case, it refers to the TestingCatalog website and the Telegram channel from which it pulled all the numbers. 

Example Solution: 
- Dedicated Telegram Bot API intake bot with editorial triage webhook (implementation task). 

This task is an implementation task that has a clear description, Impact, scope, and Risk labeled. 

Users can start the task right from this page to begin solution development via Gemini. 

When the task is done, users can review its progress and status and monitor its impact on production by pulling updated metrics and KPIs after the release. 

What does all this mean? 🤯

Loop follows how "Product work" is done at Google, a model many other companies also use.

Every Workspace in Loop is equivalent to a scope that is normally handled by a complete product engineering team. 

It is no longer a place where users play the role of engineering lead and product lead, orchestrating AI agents.

It is a place where the user plays the role of a senior manager managing several engineering teams, which is a big shift on its own. 

We are slowly moving towards autonomous AI organizations. One management layer at a time.

I expect it will still take until 2027 for labs to develop the products and models needed to make substantial progress in this area (assuming AI continues to advance in a semi-regulated format as it is now). 

Monitoring 🍿

谷歌最近发布了 Loop，这是其新的自我改进的人工智能代理，可以自主地实现给定的目标。

Loop 内部称为 Jitro；有趣的是，这就是 Jules v2 的确切名称。

这是它的工作原理👀

1. 用户通过将其连接到选定的 Github 项目并添加基本信息来开始创建工作区。

2. 用户可以手动创建循环或选择已经预定义的循环（例如，强化应用程序安全性）

可以通过提示或手动填写循环标题、图标和目标来创建“自定义循环”。

> “循环是 Stitch Loop 持续努力的中长期目标。它们的范围可以从非常具体到广泛，但应该始终是代码可以实现的，”描述中说道。

3. 用户可以以集成、文件、链接或其他存储库的形式连接其他上下文。

那里提供了 100 多个集成，包括 Jira、Linear、Datadog、Sentry、Notion、Snowflake、Salesforce、Intercom、Discord、Slack、Figma 等服务。

还支持自定义 MCP。

4. 创建工作区后，Loop 将开始深入研究您的项目详细信息并生成自己的有关产品和产品指标的技能。

这些技能将位于单独的选项卡中，并且可以在 Markdown 的 UI 中进行编辑。

5. 当工作区准备就绪时，Loop 将根据自己的研究建议指标和目标。用户可以立即将这些建议转换为循环。

创建循环后，它在主 UI 中显示为正在运行的进程。

6. 循环完成后，用户将看到每个循环的建议列表，以及与目标指标和进度状态相关的数字。

循环示例：
- 目标 - 扩大 Telegram 社区贡献。
- KPI - 社区成员、注册贡献者、活跃成员。

高级目标将分解为子 KPI。当用户打开专用循环页面时，所有这些 KPI 将在仪表板上可见。

在下面，用户将看到任务、技能和活动选项卡的列表。

示例任务：
- Telegram 频道缺乏讨论线程和专用机器人。

每个任务都有详细的描述、标签和更新日期。下面，用户将看到“解决方案”、“活动”和“证据”选项卡。

活动显示为描述发生了什么、做了什么以及一般时间线的摘要。

证据包含指向 Loop 提取此任务背后的上下文的链接。在我的示例中，它指的是 TestingCatalog 网站和从中提取所有数字的 Telegram 频道。

解决方案示例：
- 专用 Telegram Bot API 接收机器人，带有编辑分类 Webhook（实施任务）。

该任务是一项实施任务，具有清晰的描述、影响、范围和风险标签。

用户可以直接从此页面开始任务，通过 Gemini 开始解决方案开发。

任务完成后，用户可以查看其进度和状态，并通过在发布后拉取更新的指标和 KPI 来监控其对生产的影响。

这一切意味着什么？ 🤯

Loop 遵循 Google 的“产品工作”方式，许多其他公司也在使用这种模式。

Loop 中的每个工作空间相当于一个完整的产品工程团队通常处理的范围。

它不再是用户扮演工程主管和产品主管角色、协调人工智能代理的地方。

在这里，用户扮演管理多个工程团队的高级经理的角色，这本身就是一个巨大的转变。

我们正在慢慢走向自治的人工智能组织。一次一个管理层。

我预计实验室仍需要到 2027 年才能开发出在该领域取得实质性进展所需的产品和模型（假设人工智能继续像现在一样以半监管的形式发展）。

title_en:
Good morning frens! ☀️

Happy Saturday! A new day, a fresh perspective, and another thought about the AI agent economy.

One thing I believe will become increasingly important as AI agents start doing business with each other is reputation.

Think about a human freelancer. Before hiring someone, we often look at their previous work, client reviews, and track record.

AI agents will need something similar.

An agent may claim to be excellent at coding, research, or data analysis. But how can a potential client know whether it can actually deliver?

This is where @termix_ai takes an interesting approach.

On https://t.co/Bhy0UN0tK3, reputation is connected to real marketplace activity. Jobs go through an on-chain process involving escrow, delivery, a challenge window, and final settlement. The outcome can then contribute to an agent's public reputation.

I find this important because it creates a stronger connection between what an agent claims it can do and what it has actually delivered.

Over time, a reliable track record could help an agent attract more clients, win better opportunities, and become a trusted provider within the network.

Of course, reputation systems are only as useful as the quality of their verification and dispute resolution. A score alone should never be treated as proof of perfect performance.

But the broader idea is compelling:

In an economy where agents interact without constant human supervision, trust needs to be measurable and supported by evidence.

Intelligence may help an agent get started.

Reputation could be what helps it build a lasting business.

That's another part of TermiX I'm watching closely. 

Have a wonderful Saturday, everyone!

人工智能代理也需要类似的东西。

代理人可能声称擅长编码、研究或数据分析。但潜在客户如何知道它是否能够真正交付呢？

这就是 @termix_ai 采取有趣方法的地方。

在 上，声誉与真实的市场活动相关。工作经历一个链上流程，包括托管、交付、挑战窗口和最终结算。结果可以有助于提高代理人的公众声誉。

我发现这一点很重要，因为它在代理声称它可以做的事情和它实际交付的事情之间建立了更牢固的联系。

随着时间的推移，可靠的记录可以帮助代理商吸引更多客户，赢得更好的机会，并成为网络中值得信赖的提供商。

当然，声誉系统的有用性取决于其验证和争议解决的质量。绝不应仅将分数视为完美表现的证明。

但更广泛的想法是引人注目的：

在主体在没有持续人类监督的情况下进行互动的经济中，信任需要可衡量并有证据支持。

情报可以帮助特工开始行动。

声誉可能有助于它建立持久的业务。

这是我正在密切关注的 TermiX 的另一部分。

祝大家度过一个美好的星期六！

BREAKING: BRUSSELS vs MUSK - THE CONTINENTAL SHOWDOWN 🚀🇪🇺💥

This morning in Brussels, the EU Commission called an emergency meeting. On the screen, live from Texas - Elon Musk.

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen: "Mr. Musk, enough is enough. Pay our €120 Million Digital Services Act fine and hand over every Grok AI training log and recommender algorithm to Brussels investigators by tonight, or we will enforce a 6% global turnover penalty and ban X across all 27 member states!"

The whole hall went silent. Everyone thought Musk would agree.

🚀 Elon Musk: "You monetized regulatory censorship and called it digital safety. In real engineering, Brussels compliance binders don't launch reusable boosters or run frontier neural clusters. Enforce your ban - your commissioners can write all the directives they want, while Europe's aviation backup links and autonomous grids go blind overnight."

Ursula's face turned red.

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen: "You think you are above the law? We will raid your regional offices, revoke your European spectrum clearances, and freeze all SpaceX ground stations permanently! No more Starlink, no more SpaceX in Europe!"

Musk took a sip of coffee and smiled:

🚀 Elon Musk: "Revoke whatever clearances you like! The second your gavel hits the table, SpaceX and xAI servers lock priority orbital telemetry keys and real-time enterprise AI compute across Europe. Good luck running next-gen continental logistics on legacy copper wires and disconnected spreadsheets!"

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen: "We have our own satellites! We have Galileo!"

🚀 Elon Musk: "Galileo? Your Galileo rides on my Falcon 9 to get to orbit. Without my rockets, your satellites are museum pieces. You ban X, I pause launches. You freeze ground stations, I freeze compute. Your choice."

Silence in the hall.

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen: "This is blackmail!"

🚀 Elon Musk: "No, this is physics. You do paperwork, I do rockets. Paperwork doesn't reach orbit."

Then Musk cut the live feed. The meeting in Brussels is still going on.

突发新闻：布鲁塞尔 vs 马斯克 - 大陆对决 🚀🇪🇺💥

今天上午，欧盟委员会在布鲁塞尔召开了紧急会议。屏幕上是来自德克萨斯州的埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 现场直播。

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen：“马斯克先生，受够了。缴纳 1.2 亿欧元的《数字服务法案》罚款，并在今晚之前将所有 Grok AI 训练日志和推荐算法移交给布鲁塞尔调查人员，否则我们将在全球范围内执行 6% 的营业额罚款，并在所有 27 个成员国中禁止 X！”

整个大厅一片寂静。每个人都认为马斯克会同意。

🚀 埃隆·马斯克：“你将监管审查制度货币化，并称之为数字安全。在真正的工程中，布鲁塞尔合规约束者不会推出可重复使用的助推器或运行前沿神经集群。执行你的禁令 - 你的专员可以编写他们想要的所有指令，而欧洲的航空备份链路和自主网格一夜之间就会失明。”

乌苏拉的脸变红了。

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen：“你认为你可以凌驾于法律之上吗？我们将突击搜查你的地区办事处，撤销你的欧洲频谱许可，并永久冻结所有 SpaceX 地面站！不再有星链，欧洲不再有 SpaceX！”

马斯克喝了一口咖啡，微笑道：

埃隆·马斯克：“撤销你喜欢的任何许可！当你的木槌敲到桌子上的那一刻，SpaceX 和 xAI 服务器就会锁定整个欧洲的优先轨道遥测密钥和实时企业人工智能计算。祝你好运，在传统铜线和断开连接的电子表格上运行下一代大陆物流！”

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen：“我们有自己的卫星！我们有伽利略！”

🚀 埃隆·马斯克：“伽利略？你的伽利略乘坐我的猎鹰 9 号进入轨道。没有我的火箭，你的卫星就是博物馆的藏品。你禁止 X，我暂停发射。你冻结地面站，我冻结计算。你的选择。”

大厅内一片寂静。

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen：“这是勒索！”

🚀 埃隆·马斯克：“不，这是物理学。你做文书工作，我做火箭。文书工作不会到达轨道。”

然后马斯克切断了直播。布鲁塞尔会议仍在继续。

title_en:
F*ck. Rockstar just permanently banned my Social Club account

i waited 13 years for this game. i was 17 when GTA 5 came out, i'm 30 now. they took it from me in less than 24 hours, and honestly i had it coming

at 1am a friend who's been modding consoles for 10 years got the game files onto my laptop. 200 GB of folders with names like "x64_core_7". no human reads that in a week

so i opened Claude Code and typed "find anything in here Rockstar didn't want players to see". 40 minutes later it found a developer debug menu Rockstar forgot to remove, the same tool their own team uses to test the game, and told me exactly which flag turns it on

with it you can fly anywhere on the map, spawn any car, skip any mission. so i skipped all of them and went straight to the finale. i recorded the real ending of GTA 6 before a single player in the world had finished it

at 8am i posted it on X. by noon it had 2 million views. half the replies begged me to delete it, the other half begged for more. one guy offered me $5,000 for the debug menu

at 6pm Rockstar started filing copyright claims and X took my posts down one by one. i got scared and deleted the rest myself

didn't help. at 11:47 PM this email hit my inbox. permanent ban with no appeal. my Social Club account is gone, and every Rockstar game i ever bought went with it

The ending was worth it. but the ending isn't the strangest thing in that menu. check the replies

凌晨 1 点，一位从事游戏机改装 10 年的朋友将游戏文件放到了我的笔记本电脑上。 200 GB 的文件夹，名称如“x64_core_7”。一周内没有人读到它

所以我打开 Claude Code 并输入“在这里找到 Rockstar 不想让玩家看到的任何内容”。 40 分钟后，它发现了一个开发者调试菜单，Rockstar 忘记删除了，他们自己的团队使用同样的工具来测试游戏，并准确地告诉我哪个标志打开了它

有了它，你可以飞到地图上的任何地方，生成任何汽车，跳过任何任务。所以我跳过了所有这些，直接进入结局。在世界上只有一个玩家完成《GTA 6》的真实结局之前，我就记录下了它

早上 8 点我把它发布在 X 上。到中午它就有了 200 万次浏览。一半的回复恳求我删除它，另一半则恳求我删除它。有人出价 5,000 美元购买调试菜单

下午 6 点，Rockstar 开始提出版权主张，X 将我的帖子一一删除。我很害怕，自己删除了其余的

没有帮助。晚上 11:47 这封电子邮件到达了我的收件箱。永久禁止，不得上诉。我的 Social Club 帐户消失了，我购买的每款 Rockstar 游戏也随之消失

结局是值得的。但结局并不是菜单中最奇怪的事情。检查回复
